SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
COLONOSCOPY AND THERAPEUTIC ENDOSCOPY REPORT
Date of service: November 8, 2026
Endoscopist: A. Synthetic, MD (fictional)
Procedure: Colonoscopy with balloon dilation and polypectomy
Clinical indication and interval history
The patient has ileocolonic Crohn disease and underwent an ileocecal resection in 2017. She reports postprandial cramping.
Pertinent records reviewed before the examination
A colonoscopy from January 2024 described a narrowed anastomosis and a 4 mm rectal polyp that was removed at that earlier encounter. No dilation was carried out in 2024.
Procedure technique and chronological findings
The patient was positioned in the left lateral decubitus position. The colonoscope was introduced through the anus and advanced to the ileocolonic anastomosis.
Ileocolonic anastomosis and balloon dilation
A short anastomotic stricture was present. A through-the-scope balloon was advanced across the stricture and inflated to 15 mm. The colonoscope then traversed the treated narrowing into the neo-terminal ileum.
Descending colon: cold-snare polypectomy
A 9 mm sessile polyp in the descending colon was removed with a cold snare and retrieved.
Postprocedure impression
1. Crohn disease of the anastomosis.
Recovery instructions and management plan
Advance the diet as tolerated. Surveillance colonoscopy in 3 years.
